newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia posts 600.7 mln rgt trade surplus in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia posts 600.7 mln rgt trade surplus in Aug.

text.p: Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of 600.7 million ringgit in August, versus a revised deficit of 614.97 million ringgit in July 1996, the Statistics Department said on Wednesday.
Previously, the department had said the July trade gap was 624.5 million ringgit. In August 1995, Malaysia had a 1.14 billion ringgit trade deficit.
The August 1996 trade figure was in line with market expectations of a 500-600 million ringgit surplus.
Exports in August 1996 totalled 17.217 billion ringgit while imports totalled 16.616 billion ringgit, the national Bernama news agency quoted the department as saying.

The department said that for the first eight months of this year, Malaysia recorded a trade deficit of 835.475 million ringgit compared with a deficit of 8.050 billion ringgit in the first eight months of 1995.
It added that the reduced trade deficit was a result of higher export growth to 129.581 billion ringgit while imports totalled 130.416 billion ringgit.
In the Jan-Aug 1995 period, exports totalled 117.646 billion ringgit while imports amounted to 125.696 billion ringgit.
The department said exports in August 1996 grew at a faster rate of 8.3 percent against imports which rose by 0.6 percent when compared with July 1996.
Electronic valves and tubes and other related items continued to be Malaysia's leading export earner, with 18.5 percent or 24 billion ringgit of total exports.
The major export destinations for Malaysia for the eight-month period were Singapore, the United States, Japan, Hong Kong and Thailand.

The biggest contributor to the increase of imports were machinery and transport equipment which rose 2.9 billion ringgit or 3.9 percent to 78.5 billion ringgit or 60.2 percent of the total import value.

Lumpy imports -- ships, boats and floating structures, aircraft and associated equipment and parts -- declined by 2.4 billion ringgit or 36.6 percent to 4.1 billion ringgit as against 6.4 billion ringgit in 1995.
